title: SAT Math 1 — Linear Equations in One Variable Quiz
question: Five SAT-style questions on linear equations in one variable, with full working.
intro: Five questions on linear equations in one variable. **Show your working before you choose or type an answer.**

questions.title: Find the expression, not x
questions.solution:
\(12x - 27\) is exactly 3 times \(4x - 9\):

\[\begin{aligned} 12x - 27 &= 3(4x - 9) \\ &= 3 \cdot 11 \\ &= \boxed{33} \end{aligned}\]

5 is the value of \(x\), not of the expression.

questions.title: Decimals
questions.solution_title: Multiply by 100 to clear the decimals

questions.title: How many solutions?
questions.prompt:
\[3(2x - 4) - x = 5x - 12\]

How many solutions does the equation have?
questions.solution:
\[\begin{aligned} 3(2x - 4) - x &= 6x - 12 - x \\ &= 5x - 12 \end{aligned}\]

Both sides are \(5x - 12\), so every \(x\) works: **infinitely many** solutions.

questions.title: Two phone plans
questions.prompt:
Plan A costs €18 a month plus €0.05 per text message.

Plan B costs €12 a month plus €0.08 per text message.

For how many text messages in a month do the two plans cost the same?
questions.solution:
\[\begin{aligned} 18 + 0.05t &= 12 + 0.08t \\ 6 &= 0.03t \\ t &= \boxed{200} \end{aligned}\]

Check: both plans cost €28 for 200 texts.

takeaway: Clear fractions and decimals first, then compare the x-terms and the constants to see one, none or infinitely many solutions.
